prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, enabling frequency measurement at the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: Optical lattice clocks combine a single clean idea, the magic-wavelength trap that cancels the light shift while holding many atoms, with an experimental realization that moved accuracy and stability to the 10^-18 regime. The idea is original, the experimental proof is unambiguous, and the consequences are broad: a prospective redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and searches for new physics. It has been reproduced and cross-compared in many independent laboratories for more than a decade, so maturity is not in doubt. Four of eight members placed it first and five placed it in their top three, and the credited pair maps neatly onto invention (Katori) and record-performance realization, including the many-body clock (Ye). As an experimentalist I weigh most the fact that the measurement result is decisive and quantitative: it is a direct, checkable improvement in precision, not an interpretation.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the clock ecosystem is wider than two names: ion-clock groups, the Sr-clock efforts at SYRTE, PTB and NIST, and the earlier magic-wavelength and Lamb-Dicke ideas all contributed, and the committee has already honoured the frequency comb (2005) and ion-trap control (2012), so a skeptic can call this incremental on honoured ground. The SI second has also not yet been redefined, and an unfavourable reading would treat that as the point at which the achievement is formally consummated. Finally, a metrology prize risks being viewed as an instrument achievement rather than a discovery, and B003 and B023 carry a stronger claim to opening a new field of physics.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks twisted bilayer graphene (B003) first as a clear discovery of new phases of matter that has spawned a large independent field, with a coherent theory-plus-experiment trio, and places the clocks fourth.
responses.response: I agree B003 is a serious candidate and I list it as my first alternative. My difference is about maturity and attribution rather than importance. Seven years on, the superconducting pairing mechanism is still unresolved and the experimental credit (the early-career leaders of the 2018 papers, Dean, Young and others in related moire systems) is much less settled than the two-name lattice-clock attribution. I would rather wait for a cleaner credit assignment than award a three-name list that Danielsson himself says omits decisive contributors. I would welcome evidence that the committee can defend the trio.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks active matter and flocking (B006) first as a new class of non-equilibrium statistical physics (Vicsek, Toner-Tu, Ramaswamy), and places the lattice clocks seventh.
responses.response: The conceptual weight of Toner-Tu, that long-range order survives in two dimensions, is real, and I do not equate my own enthusiasm for instrumentation with merit. But Mehlig concedes that quantitative confirmation of the Toner-Tu exponents is limited relative to qualitative agreement, and that other groups (Marchetti, Cates, Simha, Chaté) have strong claims. Clocks have the opposite profile: quantitatively verified to 18 digits in independent labs. I would ask Mehlig whether he regards the clock result as a measurement advance without discovery content, or whether the tests of fundamental constants and the relativistic redshift across millimetres change that view.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks Car-Parrinello ab initio molecular dynamics (B058) first as an unambiguous two-person origin with forty years of use across condensed matter, chemistry and materials science.
responses.response: The attribution for B058 is clean and the impact is genuine, and I accept that it is arguably overdue. My reservation is the physics-versus-chemistry boundary: it is a computational method building on density-functional theory, which the 1998 chemistry prize recognized, and it is not a new physical phenomenon or measurement. Only two of eight members ranked it at all. I treat B058 as a defensible but narrower choice than B024, and it does not enter my alternatives.

responses.point: Olsson ranks aberration-corrected electron optics (B001) first for its routine, field-wide impact on atomic-resolution microscopy and a natural Rose-Haider-Urban chain of design, engineering and application.
responses.response: I share Olsson's instrumentalist standard of lasting impact, and I think instrument prizes are legitimate. We differ on how often the discovery is in the instrument. B001 was ranked by Olsson alone and has the thinnest breadth of support on the shortlist, whereas the lattice clock was ranked by all eight members. I would also point out that the credited trio makes the three-person limit binding, and the STEM-corrector line she notes is not in the credit. If she can show the credit is unambiguous I will reconsider, but at present I judge B024 stronger.

responses.point: Johansson ranks the lattice clocks first with a clean two-person attribution, but his second choice is circuit QED (B043), noting the weakness of timing after the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits.
responses.response: I agree with his attribution reading, and I think his own timing worry about B043 is exactly right: a second prize in superconducting circuits so soon after 2025 and with Wallraff and Devoret complicating credit is a poor fit. I do not therefore share his enthusiasm for B043 as a runner-up, and I prefer B003 and B023 as alternatives. On the clocks we agree, and my reservation about ion clocks being only partly credited is one I hold alongside him.

uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to wait for the formal redefinition of the second before recognizing optical lattice clocks.
Whether two names fairly capture a field where Lemonde, Sterr, Hollberg, Ludlow, Hinkley and others contributed decisively.
Whether the committee will see B003 as stronger in discovery content despite unsettled credit and an unresolved pairing mechanism.
How to weigh metrology against discovery in a physics-prize context after recent recognition of the frequency comb and ion-trap clocks.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for B024 from my profile: my documented ties are to PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur and to KTH astroparticle physics, none of which involves lattice clocks or the credited names. I am in the same broad field as B035 (IceCube), which I have ranked third and which is not in my preferred configuration, and I flag that field proximity as a potential bias rather than a documented connection.
